meta.inspiration: A product manager's year in a company with a problem: four quarters, a squad, hidden facts that sponsors state wrongly, one market event and a plan for the year after.
meta.rights_note: Original scenario. The company, the people, the product and every number are invented.

company.name: Tallyhouse
company.one_liner: A B2B time-tracking and project-profitability tool for creative agencies whose growth has plateaued on one plan at one price.
company.stage: Seed-plus, losing about ₹60 lakh a quarter, with about six quarters of cash
company.market: Creative agencies in India and Southeast Asia: design studios, advertising shops, web agencies
company.business_model: A monthly subscription per account, one plan at one price.
company.product: The core product: time tracking, project budgets, invoicing and reports.
company.role: Product manager for the core product. Your squad is seven engineers, two designers and two analysts.
company.brief: The chief executive has to show a route to profit within four quarters or the next round is gone. Growth has plateaued on one plan at one price, and every team has a theory. You can see trial starts and payments, but not what happens between. You have four quarters of twelve weeks.

stakeholders.name: Farah Siddiqui
stakeholders.says: I need a route to profit I can show the board in four quarters. Tell me what gets us there.

stakeholders.name: Vikram Nair
stakeholders.says: Three network deals died on security reviews. Give me single sign-on and an audit log and I will close them.

stakeholders.name: Anjali Menon
stakeholders.says: Billing complaints are a quarter of the tickets. It is not the problem.

stakeholders.name: Imran Sheikh
stakeholders.says: Heavy users keep asking to pay for more. A usage add-on will sell itself.

stakeholders.name: Sunita Rao
stakeholders.says: One price for everybody leaves money on the table.

stakeholders.name: Prakash Hegde
stakeholders.says: The billing module has caused every outage this year and nobody wants to touch it.

stakeholders.name: Divya Rao
stakeholders.says: Trials get lost in the first session.

segments.name: Solo and small studios
segments.description: Freelancers and studios of one to five people.

segments.name: Mid-size agencies
segments.description: Agencies of six to eighty people.

segments.name: Networks and enterprise
segments.description: Networks and holding companies with many offices.

items.name: Guided set-up
items.about: Guided set-up: import clients, invite a teammate, log a first timesheet.

items.name: Three-tier packaging
items.about: Replace the single plan with three tiers: Good, Better, Best.

items.name: Usage-based add-on
items.about: A metered add-on for the heaviest users (projects, exports, storage).

items.name: Annual-plan upsell
items.about: A discount for paying annually, in the app and at renewal.

items.name: Single sign-on and audit log
items.about: Single sign-on and an audit log, which security reviews at large agencies demand. The sales head's favourite.

items.name: Billing module rewrite
items.about: Rewrite the billing module (proration, taxes, invoices) behind every outage this year. Pays down technical debt.

items.name: Accounting integrations
items.about: Sync with the three accounting tools agencies use.

items.name: Mobile timesheets
items.about: A mobile timesheet for people who bill by the hour.

items.name: Profitability dashboards
items.about: Profitability dashboards: margin by client, by project, by person.

items.name: Design system rollout
items.about: Roll out one component library across the app.

items.name: Performance and reliability sprint
items.about: A sprint on speed and uptime.

items.name: In-app upgrade flow
items.about: In-app prompts and a one-page upgrade flow at the moments people hit a limit.

items.name: Product analytics pipeline
items.about: Record every step of the funnel as events, so the team can see where people leave. Raises measurement to level 2.

hidden.label: How hard paid conversion falls when plans are repackaged
hidden.description: How hard paid conversion falls when the plans are repackaged. Sales says customers will not mind.

hidden.label: What customers will pay for a usage add-on, against what was heard
hidden.description: What customers will pay for a usage add-on, relative to what customer success heard in renewal calls.

hidden.label: Share of customer losses caused by billing errors
hidden.description: The share of customer losses that billing errors cause. Finance counts only tickets filed as billing complaints.

hidden.label: Share of the enterprise upside that single sign-on really unlocks
hidden.description: The share of the enterprise upside that single sign-on would really unlock; other things also stall large deals. Sales counts every lost deal that mentioned security.

events.name: A network of agencies leaves for a rival
events.signal: The largest customer group has gone quiet and asked for a call about security reviews.
events.body: A network with forty offices says it cannot stay without single sign-on and an audit trail.

causes.label: We lack what large buyers need

directions.label: Commit to the missing features with dates

events.name: A rival undercuts the mid tier
events.signal: Upgrades from trial are slipping and sales say prospects keep quoting a competitor's price.
events.body: A funded rival halves its price for agencies of your size.

directions.label: Repackage and sell value, do not match the price

events.name: A security scare reaches the press
events.signal: A researcher has posted about a flaw in file sharing, and trial sign-ups have dipped.
events.body: The flaw is real and already patched in your head, but nobody outside knows that.

causes.label: A rumour with nothing behind it

plans.name: Move up-market
plans.pitch: Build for large buyers: security, sign-on, support, longer deals.

plans.name: Own self-serve
plans.pitch: Make buying frictionless and win on volume.

plans.name: Reach profit
plans.pitch: Cut spend, simplify, and stop losing money.

root.prompt: Which of these do you believe is behind the plateau?

options.label: Billing errors are driving people away
The plans do not fit what people will pay
We lack what big buyers need

measurement.label: Trial starts and payments
measurement.shows: Arrivals, payments, customers and the money. Nothing in between.

measurement.label: Core events
measurement.shows: Also activated trials and the share of customers lost each quarter.

measurement.label: The full funnel
measurement.shows: Also every step and every conversion rate, by segment.

quarters.title: The runway
quarters.opening: {company} has {cash} in the bank and {hold_profit} a quarter if nothing changes: {runway}. Only {per100_solo} of every 100 solo trials end up paying, and {per100_mid} of every 100 mid-size ones. Your squad has about {road} weeks of engineering this quarter. You can see trial starts and payments, but not what happens between.

quarters.title: First results
quarters.opening: Last quarter {shipped} shipped. Profit was {profit}, {delta} on the quarter before. {learned} {pleased}

quarters.title: The shock
quarters.opening: Last quarter {shipped} shipped and profit was {profit}. Something has changed outside the product. Read the signal below, say what you think is behind it and whether you checked, and decide how to answer.

quarters.title: The term sheet
quarters.opening: The board will back one of three plans for next year. Profit last quarter was {profit}. Where you stand: usability {U}, reliability {R}, technical debt {D}, engineering trust {trust_eng}, business trust {trust_biz}.
